title: Calibrating Fluorescence Microscopy With 3D-Speckler
author: Chieh-Chang Lin
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Materials and reagents TetraSpeck Fluorescent Microspheres Size kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: T14792 ) (see General notes 1–2 ) Appropriate immersion medium [oil (e.g., Nikon, Type F), water (Mili-Q water), or silicone (e.g., Nikon, silicone immersion oil)] for the objectives you wish to calibrate

steps.title: Gather reagents and immersion medium
steps.instruction: Collect TetraSpeck Fluorescent Microspheres Size kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number T14792) and the appropriate immersion medium for the objectives you will calibrate (oil e.g., Nikon Type F, water – Mili‑Q, or silicone oil e.g., Nikon silicone immersion oil).

steps.title: Power on microscope and select objective
steps.instruction: Turn on the fluorescence microscope and choose the objective lens(s) intended for calibration.

steps.title: Mount slide with 100 nm beads
steps.instruction: Place a microscope slide containing TetraSpeck beads of 100 nm diameter on the stage, then locate a field of view (FOV) where beads are evenly distributed, not aggregated or overly crowded.

steps.title: Optimize imaging settings and acquire Z‑stack
steps.instruction: Fine‑tune focus, camera exposure time, and light‑source power for optimal signal. (Optional) Set the Z‑range to cover the full bead depth, ensuring the step interval is <200 nm. Acquire images at each desired wavelength, preferably capturing all wavelengths at the same Z‑plane for chromatic‑aberration measurements.

substeps.instruction: Adjust focus to bring beads into sharp view.
Set camera exposure and illumination power.
Define Z‑range with ≤200 nm step size.
Capture image stacks at each calibration wavelength.

steps.title: Repeat imaging at multiple locations and with larger beads
steps.instruction: Repeat the steps of locating a suitable FOV, optimizing settings, and acquiring Z‑stacks at several different positions on the 100 nm‑bead slide. Then repeat the entire sequence using a slide with larger TetraSpeck beads (e.g., 500 nm).

steps.title: Launch 3D‑Speckler in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Set the MATLAB working directory to the folder containing the “bfmatlab” directory and the 3D‑Speckler script, then run the command Open3DSpeckler (or click Run).

steps.title: Load image file(s) and set channels
steps.instruction: In 3D‑Speckler, open the bead image file (single‑ or multi‑wavelength stack). For multi‑wavelength data, select the appropriate channel wavelengths and adjust image scales; for single‑wavelength data, add additional wavelength images when prompted.

steps.title: Choose analysis pipeline and options
steps.instruction: Select the Particle Analysis pipeline. Configure analysis options: enable Local Background Correction (default 15 % larger bounding box), Exclude Overlapping Particles, set Bounding Box Buffer (default 0.3), and activate Sort by X < Y < Z FWHM. Adjust any other desired options.

steps.title: Define ROI and set detection threshold
steps.instruction: Zoom to define the region of interest (ROI) if needed, adjust image contrast, set Z‑position with the side bar, choose the channel, then click Start Analysis. Adjust the threshold bar (or bounding‑box buffer fields) until optimal particle detection is observed, and confirm by clicking SET THRESHOLD.

substeps.instruction: Set Z‑position using the right‑hand bar.
Slide the threshold bar to optimal level.

steps.title: Fit Gaussians to detected particles
steps.instruction: Choose either 2D Gaussian Fit or 3D Gaussian Fit and click Fit Gaussians. (Optional) If performing local background correction, set the background bounding‑box size (choose “1” to double the dimensions).

substeps.instruction: If desired, enable local background correction and set size = 1 (double dimensions).

steps.title: Review particles and save channel results
steps.instruction: Click the Select button, double‑click any unwanted particles within their bounding boxes to delete them, then click Save Channel Results before proceeding to the next channel.

steps.title: Analyze remaining channels
steps.instruction: Repeat steps “Define ROI and set detection threshold” through “Review particles and save channel results” for each additional fluorescence channel.

steps.title: Optional match and align particles
steps.instruction: After all channels are analyzed, click Match & Align Pts to pair corresponding beads across wavelengths and align the channels (skip if only size/intensity data are needed).

steps.title: Generate chromatic‑aberration calibration
steps.instruction: Click Aberrations, select the wavelength(s) for which aberrations are to be measured, and press Generate to create polynomial calibration surfaces or affine transformations.

steps.title: Export results and field‑dependence plots
steps.instruction: Select Export Results, choose to include Field Dependence Plots (for illumination uniformity), specify a destination folder, and confirm. 3D‑Speckler will save an Excel file, MATLAB images, and a subfolder with the plots, then display “Data Export Completed Successfully.”

steps.title: Review Excel output and compute averages
steps.instruction: Open the exported Excel file. For lateral resolution, average the tFWHM values found in columns Q and R; for axial resolution, average the iFWHM values in column V. Use tFWHM for lateral measurements and iFWHM for axial measurements as recommended.
